rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads the preceding command with jussive لا تخف; the other readers use indicative لا تخاف.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة لا تخف جزما والباقون لا تخاف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The indicative may be circumstantial of Moses while striking, or an independent statement that he does not fear.
rows.anchor: من رفع قوله لا تخاف فإنه حال من الفاعل في أضرب أي غير خائف ولا خاش

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The jussive makes the command a response to the condition: Moses should not fear pursuit or drowning.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ لا تخف جعله جواب الشرط أي أن تضرب لا تخف دركا ممن خلقك ولا تخش غرقا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With jussive لا تخف followed by لا تخشى, the clauses can continue one another; the pause-ending vowel is lengthened rather than explained by poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك إنما يجيء في ضرورة الشعر كما أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lengthening a pause-ending vowel has a Quranic parallel in 33:67 and also occurs in ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: فأضلونا السبيلا [الأحزاب: 67] وقد جاء إشباع هذه الفتحة في كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan readers except Asim use first-person singular forms for rescuing, promising, and providing; others use plural ن.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم قد أنجيتكم وواعدتكم ورزقتكم وقرأ الباقون قد أنجيناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jafar, Abu Amr, Yaqub, and Sahl read وعدناكم without alif; other readers read واعدناكم.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وسهل ووعدناكم بغير الألف والباقون بالألف

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: He prefers وعدناكم because the alleged dialectal equivalence removes the implication of two agents that واعدناكم may carry.
rows.anchor: فاللفظ لا يدل على أن الفعل من اثنين فيكون القراءة بوعد أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anjيناكم and واعدناكم are supported by the following plural verb نزلنا.
rows.anchor: فحجته قوله { ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisai reads يحل with damma on ح; other readers use kasra in both places.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي فيحل بضم الحاء من يحلل بضم اللام والباقون بالكسر في الموضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra reading evokes what is permissible or unrestrained; the phrase describes wrath descending after having been withheld.
rows.anchor: فمعنى يحل عليكم ينزل بكم وينالكم بعدما كان ذا حظر وحجر ومنع عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damma reading treats wrath as punishment befalling people, since punishment follows wrath.
rows.anchor: لما كان تتبعه العقوبة والعذاب جعله بمنزلة العذاب فقال يحل أي ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yabis means dry; its plural forms include iyas and, with a still ب, yubus.
rows.anchor: اليبس اليابس وجمعه إياس وجمع اليبس بسكون الباء يبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asaf denotes either the severest anger or grief.
rows.anchor: والأسف أشد الغضب ويكون أيضا بمعنى الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, هم أولاء can be subject and predicate, or أولاء an apposition; على أثري may be predicate, circumstantial, or a second predicate.
rows.anchor: هم أولاء مبتدأ وخبر ويجوز أن يكون أولاء بدلا من هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to lead Israel out of Egypt by night and strike the sea so it parts into a dry road.
rows.anchor: أي سر بهم ليلا من أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to strike is extended to the road because the staff makes the road, as if the road itself were struck.
rows.anchor: فعدى الضرب إلى الطريق لما دخله هذا المعنى فكأنه قد ضرب الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses need not fear Pharaoh catching him from behind or the sea drowning him; on the jussive reading, this assurance continues.
rows.anchor: أي لا تخاف أن يدركك فرعون من خلفك ولا تخشى من البحر غرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh followed by sending his troops after Israel; an omitted clause says they entered the sea before he pursued them.
rows.anchor: معناه ألحق جنوده بهم وبعث بجنوده خلفهم وفي أثرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated wording magnifies the calamity and refers to the well-known drowning; Abu al-Najm illustrates the construction.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعظيم للأمر ومعناه غشيهم الذي عرفتموه وسمعتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Najm's repeated “my poetry” means the poetry his audience has heard and knows.
rows.anchor: أنا أبو النجم وشعري شعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Najm's repeated “my poetry” means the poetry his audience has already heard and knows.
rows.anchor: أي شعري الذي سمعت به وعلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh perished and Moses was saved, an outcome offered as a lesson to observers.
rows.anchor: أي هلك فرعون ونجى موسى هذا كان عاقبة أمرهم فليعتبر المعتبرون بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh persistently led his people away from guidance; the statement refutes his claim to show them the right path.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال وما هدى بعد قوله أضل ليتبين أنه استمر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Israel from Pharaoh in their sight and promised Moses the Mount's right side after the drowning, where he would receive the Torah and its laws.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الله تعالى وعد موسى بعد أن أغرق فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manna and quails were sent during the wilderness wandering; their account appeared earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: يعني في التيه وقد مر بيان ذلك في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative to eat good provisions functions as permission.
rows.anchor: صورته صورة الأمر والمراد به الإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of transgressing in the provision is consuming it in a forbidden way.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تتعدوا فيه فتأكلوه على الوجه المحرم عليكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is not to cross from permitted food into forbidden food.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المعنى لا تتجاوزوا عن الحلال إلى الحرام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation forbids using lawful provision to aid disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تتناولوا من الحلال للاستعانة به على المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the standard reading, God's wrath becoming due means His punishment is incumbent on them.
rows.anchor: أي فيجب عليكم عقوبتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With damma on ح, the phrase means that God's punishment descends upon them.
rows.anchor: ومن ضم الحاء فالمعنى فينزل عليكم عقوبتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever falls from a height has perished, hence the warning that the one reached by wrath has fallen; another view says he falls into Hell, and al-Zajjaj says he reaches the Abyss.
rows.anchor: أي هلك لأن من هوى من علو إلى أسفل فقد هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaffar is an intensive form derived from forgiveness; repentance is from shirk, faith is in God and His messenger, and righteous deeds fulfill obligations.
rows.anchor: وهو فعال من المغفرة { لمن تاب } من الشرك { وآمن } بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance after repentance means remaining in faith until death and persevering in it.
rows.anchor: أي ثم لزم الإيمان إلى أن يموت واستمر عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One explanation of then being guided is having no doubt about one's faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ثم لم يشك في إيمانه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas, also related from al-Rabi ibn Anas, is following the Prophet's Sunna and avoiding innovation.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ بسنة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسلك سبيل البدعة عن ابن عباس أيضا والربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir interprets guidance as loyalty to the Prophet's Household and says worship without that loyalty ends in Hell; al-Haskani and al-Ayyashi transmit this report.
rows.anchor: ثم اهتدى إلى ولايتنا أهل البيت ع فوالله لو أن رجلا عبد الله عمره

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses and his people had agreed to arrive at the appointed time together.
rows.anchor: كانت المواعدة أن يوافي الميعاد هو وقومه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Moses was to attend with leading people; eager for God, he went ahead and left them to catch up.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مع جماعته من وجوه قومه وهو متصل بقوله { وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks why Moses left his people and arrived alone.
rows.anchor: أي بأي سبب خلفت قومك وسبقتهم وجئت وحدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says his people are behind him and will soon catch up.
rows.anchor: أي هؤلاء من ورائي يدركونني عن قريب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets Moses' answer to mean that his people follow his religion and way.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه هم على ديني ومنهاجي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A second report from Hasan says they are waiting to learn what Moses brings, rather than following behind him.
rows.anchor: هم ينتظرون من بعدي ما الذي آتيهم به وليس يريد أنهم يتبعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hurried out of eagerness for God's approval, seeking to add approval to what he already had.
rows.anchor: أي سبقتهم إليك حرصا على تعجيل رضاك أي لأزداد رضا إلى رضاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested Israel after Moses departed through the calf affair and compelled them to reflect that it was no deity.
rows.anchor: أي امتحناهم وشددنا عليهم التكليف بما حدث فيهم من أمر العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses left, God tested Israel; the Samiri led them astray by calling them to error, which they accepted. This distinguishes divine testing from human misguidance.
rows.anchor: فأضاف الضلال إلى السامري والفتنة إلى نفسه ليدل سبحانه على أن الفتنة غير الضلال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God treated them as subjects under test to reveal the sincere and hypocritical to others.
rows.anchor: عاملناهم معاملة المختبر المبتلي ليظهر لغيرنا المخلص منهم من المنافق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes Moses as returning intensely angry and sorrowful.
rows.anchor: أي رجع موسى من الميقات إلى بني إسرائيل شديد الغضب حزينا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains أسفا as being distressed or anguished.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جزءا عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says Moses was regretful at what he had missed, fearing he could no longer repair his people's situation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: متحسرا متلهفا على ما فاته لأنه خشي أن لا يمكنه تدارك أمر قومه عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: One good promise was the Torah, by which Israel could learn, practice its teachings, and merit reward.
rows.anchor: أي صدقا لإيتاء الكتاب وهو التوراة لتعلموا ما فيه وتعلموا به فتستحقوا الثواب عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations of the good promise are rescue from Pharaoh and arrival at the Mount, forgiveness for repentant people, or future reward for holding to the religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الوعد الحسن هو ما وعدهم به من النجاة من فرعون ومجيئهم إلى جانب الطور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies the good promise as the hereafter's reward for adhering to God's religion in worldly life.
rows.anchor: هو ما وعدهم به في الآخرة على التمسك بدينه في الدنيا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elapsed covenant refers to the period Moses was away from them.
rows.anchor: أي مدة مفارقتي إياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their calf worship could make them deserve divine anger; the question asks whether they meant to cause that anger.
rows.anchor: بعبادتكم العجل والمعنى أم أردتم أن تصنعوا صنعا يكون سببا لغضب ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They broke their promise to Moses to maintain affairs well after him; his rebuke in 7:150 supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أي ما وعدتموه لي من حسن الخلافة بعدي ويبين ذلك قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they broke their promise by refusing to follow Moses to the appointed meeting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن إخلافهم موعده أنه أمرهم اللحاق به فتركوا المسير على أثره للميقات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says Moses ordered them to follow Aaron, obey him, and follow his instructions until Moses returned, but they disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أنه أمرهم أن يتمسكوا بطريقة هارون وطاعته ويعملوا بأمره إلى أن يرجع فخالفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Basran readers other than Sahl read تخلفه with kasra; al-Darir and al-Hasan read نخلفه with nūn and kasra; others read تخلفه with fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل البصرة غير سهل لن تخلفه بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: اخلف takes two objects: in this construction the promise is delivered to Moses by God or Moses and will not be delayed or escaped.
rows.anchor: أخلفت يتعدى إلى مفعولين لن تخلفه مثل لن تخلفه مثل لن تعطاه

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the reading as “you will find it unfulfilled,” like al-A'sha's verse; he calls it a threat, while the first reading is clearer.
rows.anchor: معناه لن تصادفه مخلفا كقول الأعشى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads نخلفه, meaning God will not fail to give Moses what was promised or diminish the agreed allotment.
rows.anchor: وأما نخلفه بالنون فالمعنى لن نخلفك إياه أي لن ننقص منه ما عقدناه لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jafar, Ali, and Ibn Abbas read لنحرقنه with light ر and still ح; other readers differ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر لنحرقنه بفتح النون وسكون الحاء وتخفيف الراء

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni relates this reading to gnashing teeth in anger and to filing metal until it flakes; Zuhayr's word يحرق illustrates the root.
rows.anchor: قال زهير: أبى الضيم والنعمان يحرق نابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads blowing into the Trumpet with nūn; others read with yā and a fatḥa on ف.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو يوم ننفخ في الصور بالنون والباقون ينفخ بالياء وفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noncanonical readings include Abu Haywa's لا مساس, Mujahid and Qatada's وسع كل شيء علما, and Ibn Ayyad's vocalization of the و in الصور with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة أبي حيوة لا مساس وقرأ مجاهد وقتادة وسع كل شيء علما

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni analyzes لا مساس as a quoted expression of refusal to approach; لا negates the saying rather than governing the noun directly.
rows.anchor: ولا يدخل على هذا الضرب من الكلام ما النافية بالنكرة فلا إذا في قوله لا مساس

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: The construction assumes an omitted “I say,” as in “no hamam for me,” because command-form nouns cannot combine directly with negation.
rows.anchor: فكأنه حكاية قول القائل مساس فكأنه قال لا أقول مساس

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains وسع كل شيء علما as God's knowledge penetrating every hidden, compact thing and opening it into a vast expanse.
rows.anchor: أنه خرق كل مصمت بعلمه لأنه بطن كل مخفي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says people claim they remained only an evening or its morning after the grave's punishment ends and God restores them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم قالوا ذلك بعد انقطاع عذاب القبر عنهم لأن الله يعذبهم ثم يعيدهم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains will be crushed to sand and scattered by winds like chaff and dust, leaving nothing on the ground.
rows.anchor: أي يجعلها ربي بمنزلة الرمل ثم يرسل عليها الرياح فيذريها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the mountains become scattered dust.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يصيرها كالهباء

rows.speaker: الرجل من ثقيف
rows.claim: A man from Thaqif asked the Prophet how mountains would fare despite their size; the answer says God makes them like sand and winds disperse them.
rows.anchor: إن الله يسوقها بأن يجعلها كالرمال ثم يرسل عليها الرياح فتفرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After scattering the mountains, God leaves their former places as smooth, level ground.
rows.anchor: أي فيدع أماكنها من الأرض إذا نسفها { قاعا } أي أرضا ملساء

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i explains qāʿ as ground left uncovered.
rows.anchor: وقيل: منكشفة عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣafṣaf is level ground without a trace of mountains; another view makes qāʿ and ṣafṣaf synonyms for level, plantless ground, from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
rows.anchor: أي أرضا مستوية ليس للجبل فيها أثر

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The terrain has neither a depression nor an elevation.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها منخفض ولا مرتفع عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan distinguishes عوج as lower ground and أمت as raised hills.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: العوج ما انخفض من الأرض والأمت ما ارتفع من الروابي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as no valley or hill.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا ترى فيها واديا ولا رابية عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads فلا يخف as jussive; other readers read فلا يخاف as indicative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فلا يخف بالجزم والباقون فلا يخاف بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub reads أن نقضي with nūn and accusative وحيه; the other readers use يَقضي with يā and nominative وحيه, with no change in meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب أن نقضي بالنون وحيه بالنصب والباقون يقضي بضم الياء وحيه بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On فلا يخف, the phrase is a prohibition; on فلا يخاف, it reports that the believer does not fear, with an implied subject and circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: من قرأ فلا يخف فإنه على النهي ومن قرأ فلا يخاف فإنه على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hams means concealed or faint speech and can describe camel hoofs; the rajaz poem uses هميس for that sound.
rows.anchor: الهمس إخفاء الكلام والصوت الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anwa means submission and humiliation or taking something by force; it can also mean yielding obedience, as the cited poets illustrate.
rows.anchor: والعنوة الخضوع والذل والعاني الأسير وأخذت الشيء عنوة أي غلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadm means diminution or loss; the root also describes a wasting abdomen and the stomach's reduction of food through digestion.
rows.anchor: والهضم النقص يقال هضمني حقي ويهضمني أي ينقصني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolve is a prior intention that prepares the self to act.
rows.anchor: والعزم الإرادة المتقدمة لتوطين النفس على الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, يومئذ modifies يتبعون, while لا عوج له is circumstantial: they follow the caller without turning away or being able to refuse.
rows.anchor: يومئذ ظرف يتبعون ولا عوج له جملة في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes “no crookedness” to describe the caller's summons, which turns aside from no one but gathers them all.
rows.anchor: أي لدعاء الداعي ولا يعدل عن أحد بل يحشرهم جميعا عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i takes it to mean that people cannot turn away from the summons; they follow quickly without looking right or left.
rows.anchor: لا يميلون عنه ولا يعدلون عن ندائه أي يتبعونه سراعا ولا يلتفتون يمينا ولا شمالا عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The voices are humbled into stillness by the majesty of the All-Merciful.
rows.anchor: أي خضعت الأصوات بالسكون لعظمة الرحمن عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd say the only sound heard is the faint noise of footsteps, like camel tread.
rows.anchor: وهو صوت الأقدام عن ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets hams as quietly spoken speech.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الهمس إخفاء الكلام عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says those who raised voices with commands and prohibitions in worldly life will be humbled to barely audible whispers.
rows.anchor: إن الأصوات العالية بالأمر والنهي في الدنيا ينخفض ويذل أصحابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession helps only someone whom God permits to intercede and whose plea He approves; eligible intercessors include prophets, saints, righteous, truthful, and martyrs.
rows.anchor: إلا شفاعة من أذن الله له في أن يشفع ورضي قوله فيها من الأنبياء والأولياء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to those following the caller; God knows all their speech and acts before and after creation, during life and after death.
rows.anchor: الضمير يرجع إلى الذين يتبعون الداعي أي يعلم سبحانه جميع أقوالهم وأفعالهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes what is before them as the afterlife and what is behind them as worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعلم ما بين أيديهم من أحوال الآخرة وما خلفهم من أحوال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot encompass God in knowledge, including His powers and all He knows.
rows.anchor: أي ولا يحيطون هم بالله علما أي بمقدوراته ومعلوماته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people cannot encompass the essence of God's greatness in His essence and acts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بكنه عظمته في ذاته وأفعاله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says people know matters before and behind them only when God reveals them.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا يحيطون علما بما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم إلا من أطلعه الله على ذلك عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says the senses cannot perceive God so that knowledge could encompass Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ولا يدركونه بشيء من الحواس حتى يحيط علمهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; face stands for its owner because humiliation appears on it.
rows.anchor: والمراد خضع أرباب الوجوه وأستسلموا الحكم للحي الذي لم يمت ولا يموت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, faces means leaders, rulers, and kings, who lose their power and dignity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالوجوه الرؤساء والقادة والملوك أي يذلون وينسلخون عن ملكهم وعزهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Whoever brings associationism to resurrection has lost God's reward.
rows.anchor: أي وقد خاب عن ثواب الله من حمل شركا إلى يوم القيامة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that anyone arriving at resurrection an unbelieving wrongdoer loses the reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قد خسر الثواب من جاء يوم القيامة كافرا ظالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who performs any obedience while believing in God is safe, since obedience without faith brings no benefit.
rows.anchor: أي ومن يعمل شيئا من الطاعات { وهو مؤمن } عارف بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a believer will not be assigned an unearned sin or have a good deed diminished.
rows.anchor: ولا أن يهضم أي ينقص من حسناته عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the believer is not punished for a sin not committed and does not have an earned good deed voided.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يخاف أن يؤخذ بذنب لم يعمله ولا أن تبطل حسنة عملها عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the believer need not fear denial of recompense or a reduction in rights.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يخاف ظلما بأن لا يجزي بعمله ولا هضما بالانتقاص من حقه عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the jussive reading, the prohibition against fearing is reassurance and safety; the verse also disproves cancellation of good deeds by sins.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن الخوف أمن بالأمن وفي هذه الآية دلالة على بطلان التحابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the book as an Arabic Quran and repeated warnings in varied forms so people might avoid sin.
rows.anchor: قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, warnings aim to make Arabs avoid a punishment like that which befell earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليتقي العرب من قبل أن ينزل بهم مثل ما نزل بأولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran renews admonition and reflection by recalling God's punishment of earlier nations.
rows.anchor: أو يجدد القرآن لهم عظة واعتبارا أي يذكروا به عقاب الله للأمم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the inherited earth as the familiar earthly realm, conquered by Muhammad's community after unbelievers are expelled.
rows.anchor: هي الأرض المعروفة يرثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفتوح بعد إجلاء الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was shown the earth's eastern and western regions and his community's dominion would reach them.
rows.anchor: زويت لي الأرض فأريت مشارقها ومغاربها وسيبلغ ملك أمتي ما زوي لي منها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar identifies the inheritors as the companions of the Mahdi at the end of time, citing reports that a righteous man from the Prophet's family fills earth with justice.
rows.anchor: هم أصحاب المهدي ع في آخر الزمان ويدل على ذلك ما رواه الخاص والعام عن النبي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الحافظ
rows.claim: Al-Hakim calls Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi unknown and notes conflicting chains, including a path through abandoned Aban ibn Abi Ayyash and a disconnected report; he considers Mahdi reports sounder and explicit about the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: ومحمد بن خالد رجل مجهول واختلف عليه في إسناده

rows.speaker: محمد بن خالد الجندي
rows.claim: A report attributed through Anas says affairs and miserliness worsen, the Hour comes only upon wicked people, and there is no Mahdi except Jesus; al-Hakim questions its narrator and chains.
rows.anchor: لا يزداد الأمر إلا شدة ولا الناس إلا شحا ولا الدنيا إلا إدبارا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that if only one day remained, God would prolong it until a righteous man from his family filled earth with justice.
rows.anchor: لو لم يبق من الدنيا إلا يوم واحد لطول الله ذلك اليوم حتى يبعث فيه رجلا مني أو من أهل بيتي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A variant says the Mahdi's name matches the Prophet's and he fills earth with equity after it was filled with injustice.
rows.anchor: يواطىء اسمه اسمي يملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا كما ملئت ظلما وجورا

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet saying the Mahdi is from his descendants, from Fatima's children.
rows.anchor: المهدي من عترتي من ولد فاطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's warnings and promises of Hell for unbelievers and Paradise for believers provide enough for worshipers to reach their goal.
rows.anchor: إن في الذي أخبرناكم به مما توعدنا به الكفار من النار والخلود فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Quran and its proofs provide sufficient means to reach truth for sincere worshipers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن في هذا القرآن ودلائله { لبلاغا } أي كفاية ووصلة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b identifies the worshipers as Muhammad's community, who pray five daily prayers and fast Ramadan.
rows.anchor: قال كعب: هم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الذين يصلون الصلوات الخمس ويصومون شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad is mercy to righteous and wicked, believers and unbelievers: believers benefit in both lives, while unbelievers are spared the destruction suffered by earlier nations.
rows.anchor: رحمة للبر والفاجر والمؤمن والكافر فهو رحمة للمؤمن في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: جبرائيل
rows.claim: In a report, Gabriel says this mercy ended his fear of the outcome and led him to believe in the Prophet after God praised him as mighty and honored near the Throne.
rows.anchor: إني كنت أخشى عاقبة الأمر فآمنت بك لما أثنى الله علي بقوله { ذي قوة عند ذي العرش مكين }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes himself as a mercy bestowed as a gift.
rows.anchor: وقد قال إنما أنا رحمة مهداة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The message benefits unbelievers by inviting them to faith and lasting reward, like offering food to a hungry person even if he refuses it.
rows.anchor: أنه عرضه للإيمان والثواب الدائم وهداه وإن لم يهتد كمن قدم الطعام إلى جائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Jabrites' claim that God benefits unbelievers in no way, since the Prophet's sending is mercy to everyone addressed.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على بطلان قول أهل الجبر في أنه ليس لله على الكافر نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation states that God alone is divine and asks whether the audience will submit; the question is also understood as a command to submit.
rows.anchor: أي مستسلمون منقادون لذلك بأن تتركوا عبادة غير الله
